Q1: Phosphorous acid has known significant hazards (Tier 1) for oral ingestion and dermal/eye exposure. However, there are substantial data gaps (Tier 4) regarding its potential carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, environmental impacts, endocrine disruption, inhalation hazards, and effects on organs and systems.
Q2: Phosphorous acid is listed on the SCIL Yellow Triangle list, indicating it has identified hazard profile issues, even though it may be considered a best-in-class chemical for specific functions. It is not found on any lists of low-hazard chemicals.
Q3: Phosphorous acid is a well-defined small molecule with a good number of scientific literature references. However, its hazard profile is not yet comprehensively characterized, as indicated by the absence of evaluations by rigorous programs like IRIS or PPRTV, a moderate number of toxicity records, and significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) across most hazard classes.
